name: United Kingdom
name_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
note: Westminster Parliament legislates for the whole UK on reserved matters. Devolved legislation is covered here through the publisher's type tokens (asp, anaw, asc, nia, ssi, wsi, nisr and the rest), each a document class below. Scotland has a mixed common-law/civil-law tradition. Welsh is co-official in Wales. The UK has no codified constitution.

si.label: Statutory Instrument
si.note: SIs use 'article' or 'regulation' as the basic unit term depending on subject matter, both map to AKN section. Numbered by year and SI number, e.g. SI 2023/1234.

nisro.label: Northern Ireland Statutory Rule or Order

frbr.note: Follows legislation.gov.uk conventions: Acts cited by regnal year and chapter before 1963, by calendar year and chapter after. Each publisher type token declared as a document class is minted as the FRBR subtype, /akn/gb/act/{token}/{year}/{number}; a token not declared here is neither walked nor minted.

numbering.note: Acts cited by short title and year (e.g. 'Companies Act 2006'). Pre-1963 acts may use regnal year and chapter (e.g. '5 & 6 Eliz. 2 c. 11'). SIs cited as 'SI year/number'.

enacting_formulae.text: BE IT ENACTED by the King's most Excellent Majesty, by and with the advice and consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authority of the same, as follows:—
enacting_formulae.note: Standard form for Acts passed by both Houses (Public Bills). Used from accession of King Charles III.

enacting_formulae.text: BE IT ENACTED by the King's most Excellent Majesty, by and with the advice and consent of the Commons in this present Parliament assembled, in accordance with the provisions of the Parliament Acts 1911 and 1949, and by the authority of the same, as follows:—
enacting_formulae.note: Money Bills and bills passed under Parliament Acts procedure (Commons only — Lords consent not required). Used from accession of King Charles III.

enacting_formulae.text: BE IT ENACTED by the Queen's most Excellent Majesty, by and with the advice and consent of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authority of the same, as follows:—
enacting_formulae.note: Standard form used during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II.

core_tlcs.note: Houses of Parliament (Westminster): House of Commons (650 seats) and House of Lords (~800 members).

structuring.prompt_additions: Body-fill task only. Preserve citations, inline markup, and list numbering verbatim. Never emit structural keywords — the scaffold owns hierarchy. Render body text in the legal register of the source language; do not translate or paraphrase.

supranational_memberships.note: Founding member; permanent member of the UN Security Council (P5).

Founding member. The European Convention on Human Rights was incorporated into domestic law by the Human Rights Act 1998 (indirect transposition, not direct effect). The UK remains a member of the Council of Europe post-Brexit.
Head of the Commonwealth. The Commonwealth has no direct-effect legal instruments.
Founding member. NATO creates treaty obligations but no directly applicable domestic law.

source_adapters.name: legislation.gov.uk
source_adapters.notes: UK national legislation publisher. Serves AKN XML via /data.akn on its own type-token paths (ukpga/uksi/...); {source_path} maps our FRBR doctype to that token. `rate_limit_per_minute` is the process-wide cap on fetches to this host; the adaptive pace starts at that cap and backs off on 429, 436 or 503 (a Retry-After value when the server sends one, otherwise a longer interval), then recovers on success. The cap is the project's own choice.

validation.note: Validated against five legislation.gov.uk AKN exports (DPA 2018, Equality 2010, Housing 2004, Finance 2020, MLR 2017 SI) through the structure, resolution and effects benchmarks; act + si hierarchies exercised end-to-end through the anchor scaffolder and Bluebell round-trip.

drafting_style.note: Rules keyed on document class, matching uri_patterns and document_classes. Term sets are English-language and hold only for this jurisdiction's drafting register. Triggers are phrases that impose a penalty, not any mention of one: a power to amend a schedule of penalties names no offence and is correct.

penalty_terms: shall be liable to a fine
commits an offence and is liable

rules.message: This unit sets a penalty but names no offence it attaches to.
This unit confers a power but states no procedure for exercising it.
